newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB vacant Prairie elevator space near unchanged.
newsitem.headline: CWB vacant Prairie elevator space near unchanged.

text.p: Vacant primary elevator space remained near unchanged from the prior week while railcar unloads at Pacific ports increased slightly for the week ended March 2, the Canadian Wheat Board said.
Average vacancy in Prairie elevators was 17 percent.

Weather and equipment related problems in shipping grains and oilseeds to Pacific ports from the Prairies since early January caused vessel backlogs on the coast and tightened up vacant primary elevator space on the Prairies.
Manitoba had the least space available at 14 percent, compared to 15 percent the week before, the CWB said.

Saskatchewan elevators averaged 17 percent vacant versus 18 percent the week before and Alberta elevators had 18 percent of their space available compared with 17 percent in the previous week, the CWB said.
Vancouver reported 2,970 railcar unloads, just under a target of 3,000 hopper cars.
Prince Rupert unloads totalled 1,125 hoppers, also slightly under the target of 1,300 railcars.
Thunder Bay unloads reached 515 railcars, exceeding a target of 490 hoppers.
